researchQuestion: Which coordinate should represent Nes Lensemuseum without collapsing the kilometre-scale sorting boom, floating work environment and private former manager's residence into one point?

result.decisionSummary: Use the named museum-building geometry as the physical anchor for the seasonal museum complex. Treat the original sorting boom, floating equipment, land buildings and private Solnes residence as separate components and access objects.

rejectedAnchors.reason: Approximately 3.63 kilometres south-west of the named museum and unsupported by any museum or lense object.

rejectedAnchors.candidate: centre of the historical sorting boom
rejectedAnchors.reason: The lense extended for kilometres and changed over time; no single point can represent its complete geometry.
Brøkkerhuset and other floating structures are components with special safety and access conditions.
The former manager's house is privately owned and not the museum or public arrival point.
The address is a useful visitor control, but direct named museum-building geometry is available.

chronologyControls.layer: boom system represented by museum model

accessControls: The museum is seasonally and event-based open; current dates must be checked before visiting.
Floating buildings, lense walks, docks and machinery require explicit access and safe conditions.
River current, slippery surfaces, ropes, wires and industrial equipment are hazards.
Solnes is private and is not part of public museum access.
The 360 metre radius is not a museum, lense, river, dock, building, property, safety, event or access boundary.
